# FDG8017

> DO NOT implement both `IEnumerator<T>` and `IEnumerable<T>` on the same type. The same applies to the non-generic interfaces `IEnumerator` and `IEnumerable`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3 Collections.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG8017
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Message: Type '{0}' should not be both a collection and an enumerator

FDG8017 reports a class or struct declared in source that implements both IEnumerator and IEnumerable (the generic interfaces imply the non-generic ones) when its base class does not already implement both; the iterator classes that the compiler generates are not in source. Removing an interface from a public type changes its public API, so the fix is breaking; there is no code fix.

## From the book

In other words, a type should be either a collection or an enumerator, but not both.
